content.summary: Saudi Arabia's public investment fund would own 93.4% of video game giant EA under a buyout plan, according to the Wall Street Journal.

content.title: How a Giant Saudi Fund Will Get Majority Ownership of Electronic Arts
content.summary: Saudi Arabia's government investment fund is poised to own this much of Electronic Arts under a leveraged-buyout deal unveiled in September and detailed in a regulatory filing last month.  A consortium led by the Saudi Public Investment Fund is funding the deal to buy the videogame maker with $36.4 billion in equity, and borrowing $20 billion of debt.  PIF is rolling over an existing holding in EA that is valued at roughly $5.2 billion at the takeover price, implying it has to put up about $29 billion of new cash to reflect its final ownership stake.

content.title: Saudi Fund to Own Almost All of Electronic Arts After Buyout
